questions.q: For a real number \(y\), let \([y]\) denote the greatest integer less than or equal to \(y\). Then the function \(f(x)=\dfrac{\tan\pi[(x-\pi)]}{1+[x]^2}\) is
opts: continuous at all \(x\), but the derivative \(f'(x)\) does not exist for some \(x\)
\(f'(x)\) exist for all \(x\) but the derivative \(f''(x)\) does not exist for some \(x\)
questions.sol: \([x-\pi]\) is an integer, so \(\tan(\pi[x-\pi])=0\) and \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\): a constant function, differentiable any number of times.

questions.q: There exists a function \(f(x)\) satisfying \(f(0)=1\), \(f'(0)=-1\), \(f(x)>0\) for all \(x\) and
questions.sol: \(f(x)=e^{-x}\) satisfies all the conditions with \(f''(x)=e^{-x}>0\). If \(f''<0\) everywhere, \(f\) is concave with \(f'(0)<0\) and must become negative for large \(x\), so (b), (c), (d) are impossible.

questions.q: If \(G(x)=-\sqrt{25-x^2}\) then \(\lim\limits_{x\to1}\left(\dfrac{G(x)-G(1)}{x-1}\right)=\)
questions.sol: The limit is \(G'(1)\), and \(G'(x)=\dfrac x{\sqrt{25-x^2}}\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\dfrac{\ln(1+ax)-\ln(1-bx)}x\) is not defined at \(x=0\). The value which should be assigned to \(f\) at \(x=0\) so that it is continuous at \(x=0\), is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\ln(1+ax)}x\to a\) and \(\dfrac{\ln(1-bx)}x\to-b\).

questions.q: If \(f(a)=2\), \(f'(a)=1\), \(g(a)=-1\), \(g'(a)=2\) then the value of \(\lim\limits_{x\to a}\dfrac{g(x)f(a)-g(a)f(x)}{x-a}\) is
questions.sol: By L'Hôpital's rule: \(g'(a)f(a)-g(a)f'(a)=4+1\).

questions.q: \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left\{\dfrac1{1-n^2}+\dfrac2{1-n^2}+\ldots+\dfrac n{1-n^2}\right\}\) is equal to
questions.sol: The sum is \(\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2(1-n^2)}=\dfrac n{2(1-n)}\to-\dfrac12\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\sin[x]}{[x]},&[x]\ne0\\0,&[x]=0\end{cases}\) Where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\) then \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}f(x)\) equals
questions.sol: For \(-1\le x<0\): \([x]=-1\), \(f=\sin1\). For \(0\le x<1\): \(f=0\). The one-sided limits differ, so the limit does not exist.

questions.q: The set of all points where the function, \(f(x)=\dfrac x{(1+|x|)}\) is differentiable, is
questions.sol: Away from \(0\) it is a quotient of differentiable functions; at \(0\): \(\dfrac{f(h)-f(0)}h=\dfrac1{1+|h|}\to1\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\dfrac12x-1\) then, on the interval \([0,\pi]\), where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer function of \(x\).
questions.sol: \([f(x)]=-1\) on \([0,2)\) and \(0\) on \([2,\pi]\), so \(\tan[f(x)]\) jumps at \(x=2\); and \(f(2)=0\) makes \(\frac1{f(x)}\) undefined there.

questions.q: The value of \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sqrt{\frac12(1-\cos2x)}}x\)
questions.sol: The expression is \(\dfrac{|\sin x|}x\): right limit \(1\), left limit \(-1\). The limit does not exist.

questions.q: Let \([\cdot]\) denote the greatest integer function and \(f(x)=[\tan^2x]\), then
questions.sol: For \(|x|<\frac\pi4\): \(0\le\tan^2x<1\), so \(f(x)=0\) near \(0\): continuous and differentiable there with \(f'(0)=0\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=[x]\cos\left(\dfrac{2x-1}2\right)\pi\), \([\cdot]\) denotes the greatest integer function, is discontinuous at
questions.sol: At an integer \(n\), \(\cos\frac{(2n-1)\pi}2=0\), so both one-sided limits \((n-1)\cdot0\) and \(n\cdot0\) equal \(f(n)=0\). Elsewhere \([x]\) is locally constant. So \(f\) is continuous everywhere.

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\dfrac x{\sin x}\) and \(g(x)=\dfrac x{\tan x}\) where \(0<x\le1\), then in this interval
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=\dfrac{\sin x-x\cos x}{\sin^2x}>0\) (as \(\tan x>x\)) and \(g'(x)=\dfrac{\tan x-x\sec^2x}{\tan^2x}=\dfrac{\sin2x-2x}{2\sin^2x}<0\).

questions.q: \(\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{\sqrt{1-\cos2(x-1)}}{x-1}\)
opts: does not exist because the left hand limit is not equal to the right hand limit.
questions.sol: The expression is \(\dfrac{\sqrt2|\sin(x-1)|}{x-1}\): right limit \(\sqrt2\), left limit \(-\sqrt2\).

questions.q: \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{x\tan2x-2x\tan x}{(1-\cos2x)^2}\) is
questions.sol: \(\tan2x-2\tan x=\dfrac{2\tan^3x}{1-\tan^2x}\) and \((1-\cos2x)^2=4\sin^4x\): the limit is \(\dfrac{x\cdot2x^3}{4x^4}=\dfrac12\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=[x]^2-[x^2]\) (where \([y]\) is the greatest integer less than or equal to \(y\)) is discontinuous at
questions.sol: At \(x=1\): left limit \(0-0\), right limit \(1-1\), value \(0\): continuous. At \(x=0\): left limit \((-1)^2-0=1\ne0\). At any other integer \(n\), \([x^2]\) and \([x]^2\) jump by different amounts.

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=(x^2-1)|x^2-3x+2|+\cos(|x|)\) is not differentiable at
questions.sol: \(\cos|x|=\cos x\). \(f(x)=(x+1)(x-1)|x-1|\,|x-2|+\cos x\): \((x-1)|x-1|\) is differentiable at \(1\), but \(|x-2|\) is multiplied by \(x^2-1\ne0\) at \(x=2\), giving a corner there.

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be any function. Define \(g:R\to R\) by \(g(x)=|f(x)|\) for all \(x\). Then \(g\) is
questions.sol: \(|\cdot|\) is continuous, so \(|f|\) is continuous when \(f\) is. \(f(x)=x\) shows the other three fail.

questions.q: For \(x\in R\), \(\lim\limits_{x\to\infty}\left(\dfrac{x-3}{x+2}\right)^x=\)
questions.sol: \(\left(1-\dfrac5{x+2}\right)^x\to e^{-5}\).

questions.q: \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sin\{\pi\cos^2x\}}{x^2}\) equals
questions.sol: \(\sin(\pi\cos^2x)=\sin(\pi-\pi\sin^2x)=\sin(\pi\sin^2x)\), and \(\dfrac{\sin(\pi\sin^2x)}{\pi\sin^2x}\cdot\dfrac{\pi\sin^2x}{x^2}\to\pi\).

questions.q: The left hand derivative of \(f(x)=[x]\sin(\pi x)\) at \(k\), \(k\) an integer is
questions.sol: For \(x\) just below \(k\): \(f(x)=(k-1)\sin\pi x\) and \(f(k)=0\). The left derivative is \((k-1)\pi\cos k\pi=(-1)^k(k-1)\pi\). (The book key prints (b).)

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be a function defined by \(f(x)=\max\{x,x^3\}\). The set of all points where \(f(x)\) is not differentiable is
questions.sol: The graphs of \(x\) and \(x^3\) cross at \(-1,0,1\) with different slopes (\(1\) and \(3\), \(1\) and \(0\), \(1\) and \(3\)), giving corners at all three points.

questions.q: Which of following functions differentiable at \(x=0\)?
questions.sol: \(\cos|x|=\cos x\) is differentiable but \(|x|\) is not, so (a), (b) fail. \(\sin|x|\) has one-sided derivatives \(\pm1\) at \(0\), the same as \(|x|\): the difference has derivative \(0\) from both sides, the sum does not.

questions.q: The integer \(n\), for which \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{(\cos x-1)(\cos x-e^x)}{x^n}\) is a finite non-zero number is
questions.sol: \(\cos x-1\approx-\dfrac{x^2}2\) and \(\cos x-e^x\approx-x\): the numerator behaves like \(\dfrac{x^3}2\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be such that \(f(1)=3\) and \(f'(1)=6\), then \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\left(\dfrac{f(1+x)}{f(1)}\right)^{\frac1x}\) equals
questions.sol: The logarithm is \(\dfrac{\ln f(1+x)-\ln f(1)}x\to\dfrac{f'(1)}{f(1)}=2\).

questions.q: If \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{((a-n)nx-\tan x)\sin nx}{x^2}=0\), where \(n\) is non zero real number, then \(a\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{(a-n)nx-\tan x}x\cdot\dfrac{\sin nx}x\to\left[(a-n)n-1\right]n=0\), so \(a=n+\dfrac1n\).
By L'Hôpital's rule: \(\dfrac{f'(2)(2+2h)}{f'(1)(1-2h)}\to\dfrac{6\cdot2}{4\cdot1}\).

questions.q: \(f(x)\) is twice differentiable polynomial function such that \(f(1)=1\), \(f(2)=4\), \(f(3)=9\), then
opts: There exist at least one \(x\in(1,2)\) such that \(f''(x)=3\)
There exist at least one \(x\in(2,3)\) such that \(f'(x)=5=f''(x)\)
There exist at least one \(x\in(1,3)\) such that \(f''(x)=2\)
questions.sol: \(g(x)=f(x)-x^2\) vanishes at \(1,2,3\). By Rolle's theorem \(g'\) vanishes in \((1,2)\) and in \((2,3)\), hence \(g''=f''-2\) vanishes somewhere in \((1,3)\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=||x|-1|\), then points where \(f(x)\) is not differentiable is (are)
questions.sol: \(|x|\) has a corner at \(0\) (where \(|x|-1\ne0\)), and \(||x|-1|\) has corners where \(|x|=1\).

questions.q: If \(f\) is a differentiable function satisfying \(f\left(\dfrac1n\right)=0\) for all \(n\ge1\), \(n\in I\), then
questions.sol: By continuity \(f(0)=\lim f\left(\frac1n\right)=0\). As \(f'(0)\) exists, \(f'(0)=\lim\dfrac{f(1/n)-f(0)}{1/n}=0\).

questions.q: The value of \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\left((\sin x)^{1/x}+(1/x)^{\sin x}\right)\), where \(x>0\) is
questions.sol: \((\sin x)^{1/x}\to0\) (a number below \(1\) raised to a large power) and \(\left(\frac1x\right)^{\sin x}=e^{-\sin x\ln x}\to e^0=1\).

questions.q: Let \(g(x)=\dfrac{(x-1)^n}{\log\cos^m(x-1)}\); \(0<x<2\), \(m\) and \(n\) are integers, \(m\ne0\), \(n>0\), and let \(p\) be the left hand derivative of \(|x-1|\) at \(x=1\). If \(\lim\limits_{x\to1^+}g(x)=p\), then
questions.sol: \(p=-1\). With \(h=x-1\): \(\log\cos^mh\approx-\dfrac{mh^2}2\), so \(g\approx-\dfrac{2h^{n-2}}m\); a limit \(-1\) needs \(n=2\) and \(m=2\).

questions.q: The value of \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac1{x^3}\displaystyle\int_0^x\dfrac{t\ln(1+t)}{t^4+4}dt\) is
questions.sol: By L'Hôpital's rule: \(\lim\dfrac{x\ln(1+x)}{3x^2(x^4+4)}=\dfrac1{3\cdot4}\).

questions.q: If \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\left[1+x\ln(1+b^2)\right]^{1/x}=2b\sin^2\theta\), \(b>0\) and \(\theta\in(-\pi,\pi]\), then the value of \(\theta\) is
questions.sol: The limit is \(e^{\ln(1+b^2)}=1+b^2\), so \(\sin^2\theta=\dfrac{1+b^2}{2b}\ge1\): \(b=1\) and \(\sin^2\theta=1\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2\left|\cos\dfrac\pi x\right|,&x\ne0\\0,&x=0\end{cases}\), \(x\in R\), then \(f\) is
opts: differentiable at \(x=0\) but not differentiable at \(x=2\)
not differentiable at \(x=0\) but differentiable at \(x=2\)
differentiable at neither at \(x=0\) nor at \(x=2\)
questions.sol: At \(0\): \(\dfrac{f(h)}h=h\left|\cos\frac\pi h\right|\to0\). At \(2\): \(\cos\frac\pi x\) passes through \(0\) with non-zero slope, so \(\left|\cos\frac\pi x\right|\) has a corner and the left and right derivatives are \(-\pi\) and \(\pi\).

questions.q: If \(\lim\limits_{x\to\infty}\left(\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x+1}-ax-b\right)=4\), then
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{x+1}=x+\dfrac1{x+1}\), so the expression is \((1-a)x-b+\dfrac1{x+1}\): \(a=1\), \(-b=4\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha(a)\) and \(\beta(a)\) be the roots of the equation \(\left(\sqrt[3]{1+a}-1\right)x^2+\left(\sqrt{1+a}-1\right)x+\left(\sqrt[6]{1+a}-1\right)=0\) where \(a>-1\). Then \(\lim\limits_{a\to0^+}\alpha(a)\) and \(\lim\limits_{a\to0^+}\beta(a)\) are
Let \(k\in\mathbb R\). If \(\lim\limits_{x\to0^+}\left(\sin(\sin kx)+\cos x+x\right)^{\frac2x}=e^6\), then the value of \(k\) is
questions.sol: The base is \(1+(k+1)x+\ldots\), so the limit is \(e^{2(k+1)}\): \(2(k+1)=6\).

questions.q: If \(x+|y|=2y\), then \(y\) as a function of \(x\) is
questions.sol: \(y\ge0\): \(y=x\) (for \(x\ge0\)). \(y<0\): \(x=3y\), \(y=\dfrac x3\) (for \(x<0\)). So \(y\) is defined and continuous for all \(x\), with slopes \(1\) and \(\frac13\) on the two sides of \(0\) (not differentiable there). (The book's key omits this question.)

questions.q: Let \([x]\) denote the greatest integer less than (or) equal to \(x\). If \(f(x)=[x\sin\pi x]\) then \(f(x)\) is
questions.sol: For \(-1<x<1\): \(0\le x\sin\pi x<1\), so \(f=0\) on \((-1,1)\): continuous and differentiable there. Just right of \(1\), \(x\sin\pi x<0\) and \(f=-1\): discontinuous at \(1\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=1+|\sin x|\) is
opts: not differentiable at infinite number of points.
questions.sol: \(|\sin x|\) is continuous everywhere and has corners at every \(x=n\pi\) (including \(0\)). (The book key prints (b), (d).)

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}|x-3|,&x\ge1\\\dfrac{x^2}4-\dfrac{3x}2+\dfrac{13}4,&x<1\end{cases}\).
questions.sol: At \(1\): both pieces give \(2\) and both slopes are \(-1\) (\(\frac x2-\frac32\) and \(-1\)). At \(3\): \(|x-3|\) is continuous with a corner.

questions.q: Let \(g(x)\) be a function defined on \((-1,1)\). If the area of the equilateral triangle with two of its vertices at \((0,0)\) and \((x,g(x))\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}4\) then the function \(g(x)\) is,
questions.sol: The side is \(1\): \(x^2+g(x)^2=1\), so \(g=\sqrt{1-x^2}\) or \(g=-\sqrt{1-x^2}\) ((a) is not a single-valued function).

questions.q: Which of the following functions are continuous on \((0,\pi)\) ?
questions.sol: \(\tan x\) breaks at \(\frac\pi2\). An integral with a bounded integrand is continuous. In (c), at \(\frac{3\pi}4\): \(2\sin\frac\pi6=1\). In (d), at \(\frac\pi2\) the values are \(\frac\pi2\) and \(-\frac\pi2\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<0\\x^2,&x\ge0\end{cases}\) then for all \(x\)
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=0\) for \(x<0\), \(2x\) for \(x\ge0\) (and \(f'(0)=0\)): continuous, but with a corner at \(0\).

questions.q: Let \(g(x)=xf(x)\), where \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x\sin\dfrac1x,&x\ne0\\0,&x=0\end{cases}\). At \(x=0\)
opts: \(g\) is differentiable but \(g'\) is not continuous
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{f(h)}h=\sin\frac1h\) has no limit: \(f\) is not differentiable. \(g=x^2\sin\frac1x\): \(g'(0)=0\), and \(g'(x)=2x\sin\frac1x-\cos\frac1x\) has no limit at \(0\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\max\{(1-x),(1+x),2\}\), \(x\in(-\infty,\infty)\), is
opts: differentiable at all points except \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\)
continuous at all points except \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\), where it is discontinuous
questions.sol: \(f=1-x\) for \(x\le-1\), \(2\) for \(-1\le x\le1\), \(1+x\) for \(x\ge1\): continuous, with corners at \(\pm1\).

questions.q: Let \(h(x)=\min\{x,x^2\}\) for every real number of \(x\). Then
opts: \(h\) is not differentiable at two values of \(x\).
questions.sol: \(h=x\) for \(x\le0\), \(x^2\) on \([0,1]\), \(x\) for \(x\ge1\): continuous, with corners at \(0\) and \(1\), and \(h'=1\) for \(x>1\).

\(f(x)\) is not differentiable at two points
questions.sol: \(f=x^3\) for \(x\le1\) and \(1\) for \(x>1\): continuous everywhere, not differentiable only at \(x=1\) (so it is not differentiable for all \(x\)), and \(f=1>0\) for \(x>1\). (The book key prints (a), (c); (b) is also true.)

questions.q: Let \(L=\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{a-\sqrt{a^2-x^2}-\dfrac{x^2}4}{x^4}\), \(a>0\). If \(L\) is finite, then
questions.sol: \(a-\sqrt{a^2-x^2}=\dfrac{x^2}{2a}+\dfrac{x^4}{8a^3}+\ldots\) The \(x^2\) terms cancel only if \(\frac1{2a}=\frac14\), \(a=2\); then \(L=\dfrac1{8a^3}=\dfrac1{64}\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be a function such that \(f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\), \(\forall\ x,y\in R\). If \(f(x)\) is differentiable at \(x=0\), then
opts: \(f(x)\) is differentiable only in a finite interval containing zero
\(f(x)\) is differentiable except at finitely many points
questions.sol: \(f(0)=0\) and \(f'(x)=\lim\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}h=\lim\dfrac{f(h)}h=f'(0)\) for every \(x\). So \(f(x)=f'(0)x\): differentiable everywhere with constant derivative.

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\begin{cases}-x-\dfrac\pi2,&x\le-\dfrac\pi2\\-\cos x,&-\dfrac\pi2<x\le0\\x-1,&0<x\le1\\\ln x,&x>1\end{cases}\), then
questions.sol: At \(-\frac\pi2\) both pieces give \(0\). At \(0\): values \(-1,-1\) but slopes \(\sin0=0\) and \(1\). At \(1\): values \(0,0\) and slopes \(1,1\). \(-\frac32\) lies inside \(\left(-\frac\pi2,0\right)\), where \(-\cos x\) is smooth.

questions.q: For every integer \(n\), let \(a_n\) and \(b_n\) be real numbers. Let function \(f:R\to R\) be given by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}a_n+\sin\pi x,&\text{for }x\in[2n,2n+1]\\b_n+\cos\pi x,&\text{for }x\in(2n-1,2n)\end{cases}\) for all integers \(n\). If \(f\) is continuous, then which of the following hold(s) for all \(n\)?
For \(a\in R\) (the set of all real numbers), \(a\ne-1\), \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{(1^a+2^a+\ldots+n^a)}{(n+1)^{a-1}[(na+1)+(na+2)+\ldots+(na+n)]}=\dfrac1{60}\). Then \(a=\)
questions.sol: For \(a>-1\) the numerator behaves like \(\dfrac{n^{a+1}}{a+1}\) and the denominator like \(n^{a+1}\left(a+\frac12\right)\): \((a+1)(2a+1)=120\), \(a=7\) or \(-\frac{17}2\). For \(a=-\frac{17}2\) the numerator tends to a constant while the denominator tends to \(0\), so the limit is not \(\frac1{60}\). Only \(a=7\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[a,b]\to[1,\infty)\) be a continuous function and let \(g:R\to R\) be defined as \(g(x)=\begin{cases}0,&\text{if }x<a\\\displaystyle\int_a^xf(t)dt,&\text{if }a\le x\le b\\\displaystyle\int_a^bf(t)dt,&\text{if }x>b\end{cases}\) Then
opts: \(g(x)\) is continuous but not differentiable at \(a\)
\(g(x)\) is continuous but not differentiable at \(b\)
\(g(x)\) is continuous and differentiable at either \(a\) or \(b\) but not both
questions.sol: \(g\) is continuous. At \(a\) the left and right derivatives are \(0\) and \(f(a)\ge1\); at \(b\) they are \(f(b)\ge1\) and \(0\).

questions.q: For every pair of continuous function \(f,g:[0,1]\to R\) such that \(\max\{f(x):x\in[0,1]\}=\max\{g(x):x\in[0,1]\}\), the correct statement(s) is(are):
questions.sol: Let \(h=f-g\). Where \(f\) attains the common maximum \(h\ge0\), where \(g\) attains it \(h\le0\); so \(h(c)=0\) for some \(c\), i.e. \(f(c)=g(c)\). Then (a) and (d) hold; (b), (c) fail e.g. for \(f=g=1\).

questions.q: Let \(g:R\to R\) be a differentiable function with \(g(0)=0\), \(g'(0)=0\) and \(g'(1)\ne0\). Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac x{|x|}g(x),&x\ne0\\0,&x=0\end{cases}\) and \(h(x)=e^{|x|}\) for all \(x\in R\). Let \((foh)(x)\) denote \(f(h(x))\) and \((hof)(x)\) denote \(h(f(x))\). Then which of the following is (are) true?
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{f(x)}x=\dfrac{g(x)}{|x|}\to0\) since \(g'(0)=0\): (a). \(e^{|x|}\) has a corner at \(0\). \(f(h(x))=g\left(e^{|x|}\right)\) has one-sided derivatives \(\pm g'(1)\ne0\). \(h(f(x))=e^{|g(x)|}\) and \(\dfrac{|g(x)|}x\to0\): differentiable.

questions.q:
Let \(f,g:[-1,2]\to R\) be continuous functions which are twice differentiable on the interval \((-1,2)\). Let the values of \(f\) and \(g\) at the points \(-1,0\) and \(2\) be as given in the following table.
\(x=-1\)\(x=0\)\(x=2\)
\(f(x)\)\(3\)\(6\)\(0\)
\(g(x)\)\(0\)\(1\)\(-1\)
In each of the intervals \((-1,0)\) and \((0,2)\), the function \((f-3g)''\) never vanishes. Then the correct statement(s) is(are)
opts: \(f'(x)-3g'(x)=0\) has exactly two solutions in \((-1,0)\) and exactly two solutions in \((0,2)\)
questions.sol: \(h=f-3g\) takes the value \(3\) at \(-1,0,2\). By Rolle's theorem \(h'\) vanishes at least once in each interval; a second zero in the same interval would make \(h''\) vanish there. So exactly one in each.

questions.q: Let \(f:\left[-\dfrac12,2\right]\to R\) and \(g:\left[-\dfrac12,2\right]\to R\) be functions defined by \(f(x)=[x^2-3]\) and \(g(x)=|x|f(x)+|4x-7|f(x)\), where \([y]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(y\) for \(y\in R\). Then
opts: \(f\) is discontinuous exactly at three points in \(\left[-\dfrac12,2\right]\)
\(f\) is discontinuous exactly at four points in \(\left[-\dfrac12,2\right]\)
\(g\) is not differentiable exactly at four points in \(\left(-\dfrac12,2\right)\)
\(g\) is not differentiable exactly at five points in \(\left(-\dfrac12,2\right)\)
questions.sol: \([x^2]\) jumps where \(x^2=1,2,3,4\): \(x=1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3,2\) — four points. \(g=(|x|+|4x-7|)f\) is discontinuous at \(1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3\) and has a corner at \(0\) (\(f(0)=-3\)); at \(x=\frac74\), \(f=0\) nearby so \(g\) is smooth. Four points in the open interval.

questions.q: Let \(a,b\in R\) and \(f:R\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=a\cos(|x^3-x|)+b|x|\sin(|x^3+x|)\). Then \(f\) is
questions.sol: \(\cos|u|=\cos u\), and \(|x|\sin|x^3+x|=|x|\sin\left(|x|(x^2+1)\right)=x\sin(x^3+x)\) (both factors change sign together). So \(f(x)=a\cos(x^3-x)+bx\sin(x^3+x)\) is differentiable everywhere for all \(a,b\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to(0,1)\) be a continuous function. Then, which of the following function(s) has (have) the value zero at some point in the interval \((0,1)\)?
questions.sol: (a) negative at \(0\), positive at \(1\). (b) always positive. (c) negative at \(0\); at \(1\) it exceeds \(1-\sin\left(\frac\pi2-1\right)>0\). (d) \(\ge e^x-x>0\). By the intermediate value theorem (a) and (c) vanish in \((0,1)\).

questions.q: Let \([x]\) be the greatest integer less than or equals to \(x\). Then, at which of the following point(s) the function \(f(x)=x\cos(\pi(x+[x]))\) is discontinuous?
questions.sol: At an integer \(n\): right limit \(n\cos2n\pi=n\), left limit \(n\cos(2n-1)\pi=-n\). These differ unless \(n=0\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\dfrac{1-x(1+|1-x|)}{|1-x|}\cos\left(\dfrac1{1-x}\right)\) for \(x\ne1\). Then
questions.sol: \(x<1\): \(f=\dfrac{(1-x)^2}{1-x}\cos\dfrac1{1-x}=(1-x)\cos\dfrac1{1-x}\to0\). \(x>1\): \(f=\dfrac{1-x^2}{x-1}\cos\dfrac1{1-x}=-(1+x)\cos\dfrac1{1-x}\), which oscillates.

questions.q:
For any positive integer \(n\), define \(f_n:(0,\infty)\to R\) as \(f_n(x)=\sum\limits_{j=1}^n\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac1{1+(x+j)(x+j-1)}\right)\) for all \(x\in(0,\infty)\)
(Here, the inverse trigonometric function \(\tan^{-1}x\) assumes values in \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\).) Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
questions.sol: \(f_n(x)=\tan^{-1}(x+n)-\tan^{-1}x\), so \(\tan f_n(x)=\dfrac n{1+x(x+n)}\to0\) and \(\sec^2f_n\to1\): (c) false, (d) true. The domain is \((0,\infty)\), so \(f_j(0)\) and \(f_j'(0)\) in (a), (b) are not defined — the official answer is (d) only.

questions.q: Let \(f:(0,\pi)\to R\) be a twice differentiable function such that \(\lim\limits_{t\to x}\dfrac{f(x)\sin t-f(t)\sin x}{t-x}=\sin^2x\) for all \(x\in(0,\pi)\). If \(f\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)=-\dfrac\pi{12}\), then which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
questions.sol: The limit is \(f(x)\cos x-f'(x)\sin x=\sin^2x\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{\sin x}\right)'=-1\), so \(f(x)=(C-x)\sin x\) and the data give \(C=0\): \(f(x)=-x\sin x\). (a) \(f\left(\frac\pi4\right)=-\frac\pi{4\sqrt2}\). (b) is \(\sin x>x-\frac{x^3}6\): true. (c) \(f'=-\sin x-x\cos x=0\) when \(\tan x=-x\), which has a root in \(\left(\frac\pi2,\pi\right)\). (d) \(f''=-2\cos x+x\sin x\): \(\frac\pi2-\frac\pi2=0\).

questions.q:
Let \(f:R\to R\) be a function. We say that \(f\) has
PROPERTY 1 if \(\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(h)-f(0)}{\sqrt{|h|}}\) exists and is finite, and
PROPERTY 2 if \(\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(h)-f(0)}{h^2}\) exists and is finite.
Then which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.sol: (a) \(\dfrac{h^{2/3}}{|h|^{1/2}}=|h|^{1/6}\to0\). (b) \(\dfrac{\sin h}{h^2}\) is unbounded. (c) \(\dfrac{|h|}{\sqrt{|h|}}\to0\). (d) \(\dfrac{h|h|}{h^2}=\pm1\): no limit.

questions.q: For \(a\in R\), \(|a|>1\), let \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(\dfrac{1+\sqrt[3]2+\ldots+\sqrt[3]n}{n^{7/3}\left(\dfrac1{(an+1)^2}+\dfrac1{(an+2)^2}+\ldots+\dfrac1{(an+n)^2}\right)}\right)=54\). Then the possible value(s) of \(a\) is/are
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1{n^{4/3}}\sum k^{1/3}\to\displaystyle\int_0^1x^{1/3}dx=\frac34\) and \(n\sum\dfrac1{(an+k)^2}\to\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{dx}{(a+x)^2}=\dfrac1{a(a+1)}\). So \(\frac34a(a+1)=54\), \(a^2+a-72=0\).

questions.q: Let the function \(f:R\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=x^3-x^2+(x-1)\sin x\) and let \(g:R\to R\) be an arbitrary function. Let \(fg:R\to R\) be the product function defined by \((fg)(x)=f(x)g(x)\). Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: If \(g\) is continuous at \(x=1\), then \(fg\) is differentiable at \(x=1\).
If \(fg\) is differentiable at \(x=1\), then \(g\) is continuous at \(x=1\).
If \(g\) is differentiable at \(x=1\), then \(fg\) is differentiable at \(x=1\).
If \(fg\) is differentiable at \(x=1\), then \(g\) is differentiable at \(x=1\)
questions.sol: \(f(1)=0\), \(f'(1)=1+\sin1\ne0\). \(\dfrac{(fg)(1+h)-0}h=\dfrac{f(1+h)}h\,g(1+h)\to f'(1)g(1)\) when \(g\) is continuous at \(1\): (a), hence (c). Conversely only \(\lim g(1+h)\) is forced; \(g(1)\) itself can be anything, so (b), (d) fail.

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) and \(g:R\to R\) be functions satisfying \(f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+f(x)f(y)\) and \(f(x)=xg(x)\) for all \(x,y\in R\). If \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}g(x)=1\), then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
opts: If \(g(0)=1\), then \(g\) is differentiable at every \(x\in R\)
questions.sol: \(f(0)=0\) and \(f'(x)=\lim\dfrac{f(h)(1+f(x))}h=1+f(x)\) (as \(\frac{f(h)}h=g(h)\to1\)). So \(f(x)=e^x-1\): \(f'(0)=1\), \(f'(1)=e\). \(g(x)=\dfrac{e^x-1}x\) with \(g(0)=1\) is differentiable everywhere (\(g'(0)=\frac12\)).

questions.q:
Let \(f:\left[-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right]\to R\) be a continuous function such that \(f(0)=1\) and \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac\pi3}f(t)dt=0\)
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: The equation \(f(x)-3\cos3x=0\) has at least one solution in \(\left(0,\dfrac\pi3\right)\)
The equation \(f(x)-3\sin3x=-\dfrac6\pi\) has at least one solution in \(\left(0,\dfrac\pi3\right)\)
questions.sol: (a) \(F(x)=\int_0^xf-\sin3x\) vanishes at \(0\) and \(\frac\pi3\): Rolle. (b) \(G(x)=\int_0^xf+\cos3x+\frac{6x}\pi\) equals \(1\) at both ends: Rolle. (c), (d): \(\int_0^xf\approx x\), so the limits are \(\dfrac{x^2}{-x^2}=-1\) and \(\dfrac{x\cdot x}{x^2}=1\).

questions.q: Let \(S=(0,1)\cup(1,2)\cup(3,4)\) and \(T=\{0,1,2,3\}\). Then which of the following statements is(are) true?
opts: There are infinitely many functions from \(S\) to \(T\)
There are infinitely many strictly increasing functions from \(S\) to \(T\)
The number of continuous functions from \(S\) to \(T\) is at most \(120\)
Every continuous function from \(S\) to \(T\) is differentiable
questions.sol: (a) each of infinitely many points can go to any of \(4\) values. (b) a strictly increasing function is one-one, impossible from an infinite set into \(4\) values. (c) a continuous function into a finite set is constant on each interval: \(4^3=64\). (d) such functions are locally constant, hence differentiable.

questions.q:
Let \(S\) be the set of all \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\) such that \(\lim\limits_{x\to\infty}\dfrac{\sin(x^2)(\log_ex)^\alpha\sin\left(\dfrac1{x^2}\right)}{x^{\alpha\beta}(\log_e(1+x))^\beta}=0\)
Then which of the following is (are) correct?
questions.sol: For large \(x\): \(\sin\frac1{x^2}\approx\frac1{x^2}\) and \(\log(1+x)\approx\log x\), so the expression behaves like \(\sin(x^2)\dfrac{(\log x)^{\alpha-\beta}}{x^{\alpha\beta+2}}\). It tends to \(0\) iff \(\alpha\beta+2>0\), or \(\alpha\beta+2=0\) with \(\alpha<\beta\). (a) \(-1<0\); (b) \(1>0\) ✓; (c) \(1>0\) ✓; (d) \(\alpha\beta+2=0\) but \(\alpha>\beta\).

questions.q: Evaluate the following limit \(\lim\limits_{x\to1}\left[\dfrac{x-1}{2x^2-7x+5}\right]\)
Evaluate : \(\lim\limits_{x\to1}(1-x)\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi x}2\right)\)
questions.sol: With \(h=1-x\): \(h\cot\dfrac{\pi h}2=\dfrac h{\tan\frac{\pi h}2}\to\dfrac2\pi\).

questions.q: Evaluate : \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\sqrt{\dfrac{x-\sin x}{x+\cos^2x}}\)
questions.sol: The numerator tends to \(0\) and the denominator to \(1\).

questions.q: Find \(f'(1)\) if \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x-1}{2x^2-7x+5}&\text{when }x\ne1\\-\dfrac13&\text{when }x=1\end{cases}\)
questions.sol: For \(x\ne1\), \(f(x)=\dfrac1{2x-5}\), and this also gives \(-\frac13\) at \(x=1\). So \(f'(1)=\dfrac{-2}{(2-5)^2}\).

questions.q: Evaluate \(\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{(a+h)^2\sin(a+h)-a^2\sin a}h\)
questions.sol: It is the derivative of \(x^2\sin x\) at \(x=a\).

questions.q: If \(f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\) for all \(x\) and \(y\). If the function \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\), then show that \(f\) is continuous for all \(x\).
questions.sol: \(f(0)=0\). \(\lim\limits_{h\to0}f(x+h)=f(x)+\lim\limits_{h\to0}f(h)=f(x)+f(0)=f(x)\).

questions.q: Determine the values of \(a,b,c\) for which the function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\sin(a+1)x+\sin x}x&\text{for }x<0\\c&\text{for }x=0\\\dfrac{(x+bx^2)^{1/2}-x^{1/2}}{bx^{3/2}}&\text{for }x>0\end{cases}\) is continuous at \(x=0\)
questions.sol: Left limit \(a+2\). Right limit \(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+bx}-1}{bx}\to\dfrac12\). So \(a+2=c=\frac12\).

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a twice differentiable function such that \(f''(x)=-f(x)\), \(f'(x)=g(x)\) and \(h(x)=[f(x)]^2+[g(x)]^2\) find \(h(10)\) if \(h(5)=1\)
questions.sol: \(h'=2ff'+2gg'=2fg+2g(-f)=0\), so \(h\) is constant.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}1+x,&0\le x\le2\\3-x,&2<x\le3\end{cases}\) Determine the form of \(g(x)=f(f(x))\) and hence find the points of discontinuity of \(g\) if any.
Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x^2}2,&0\le x<1\\2x^2-3x+\dfrac32,&1\le x\le2\end{cases}\) Discuss the continuity of \(f,f',f''\) on \([0,2]\)
questions.ans: \(f\) and \(f'\) are continuous on \([0,2]\); \(f''\) is discontinuous at \(x=1\)

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\) be defined in the interval \([-2,2]\) such that \(f(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&-2\le x\le0\\x-1,&0<x\le2\end{cases}\) \(g(x)=f(|x|)+|f(x)|\). Test the differentiability of \(g(x)\) in \((-2,2)\)
Let \(f(x)\) be a continuous and \(g(x)\) be a discontinuous function. Prove that \(f(x)+g(x)\) is discontinuous function.
questions.sol: If \(f+g\) were continuous, then \(g=(f+g)-f\) would be a difference of continuous functions, hence continuous — a contradiction.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\) be a function satisfying the condition \(f(-x)=f(x)\ \forall\ x\). If \(f'(0)\) exists, find the value.
questions.sol: Differentiating \(f(-x)=f(x)\) at \(0\): \(-f'(0)=f'(0)\).

questions.q: Let \(g(x)\) be a polynomial of degree one and \(f(x)\) be defined by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}g(x),&x\le0\\\left[\dfrac{(1+x)}{(2+x)}\right]^{\frac1x},&x>0\end{cases}\) Find the continuous function \(f(x)\) satisfying \(f'(1)=f(-1)\).
questions.sol: Let \(g(x)=ax+b\). As \(x\to0^+\), \(\left(\frac{1+x}{2+x}\right)^{1/x}\to0\), so \(b=0\). For \(x>0\), \(\dfrac{f'}f=-\dfrac1{x^2}\ln\dfrac{1+x}{2+x}+\dfrac1x\left(\dfrac1{1+x}-\dfrac1{2+x}\right)\); at \(x=1\): \(f'(1)=\dfrac23\left(\ln\dfrac32+\dfrac16\right)\). \(f(-1)=-a\) gives \(a\).

questions.q: Let \(R\) be the set of real numbers and \(f:R\to R\) be such that for all \(x\) and \(y\) in \(R\), \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le|x-y|^3\). Prove that \(f(x)\) is constant.
questions.sol: \(\left|\dfrac{f(x)-f(y)}{x-y}\right|\le|x-y|^2\to0\) as \(y\to x\), so \(f'(x)=0\) everywhere.

questions.q: Draw the graph of the function \(y=[x]+|1-x|\), \(-1\le x\le3\). Determine the points, if any, where this function is not differentiable.
questions.sol: \(y=-x\) on \([-1,0)\); \(1-x\) on \([0,1)\); \(x\) on \([1,2)\); \(x+1\) on \([2,3)\); \(5\) at \(x=3\). The graph consists of line segments with jumps at \(0,2,3\) and a corner at \(1\).

questions.q: Find the values of \(a\) and \(b\), so that the function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x+a\sqrt2\sin x,&0\le x<\pi/4\\2x\cot x+b,&\pi/4\le x\le\pi/2\\a\cos2x-b\sin x,&\pi/2<x\le\pi\end{cases}\) is continuous for \(0\le x\le\pi\).
questions.sol: At \(\frac\pi4\): \(\frac\pi4+a=\frac\pi2+b\). At \(\frac\pi2\): \(b=-a-b\). So \(a=-2b\) and \(-3b=\frac\pi4\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{1-\cos4x}{x^2},&x<0\\a,&x=0\\\dfrac{\sqrt x}{\sqrt{16+\sqrt x}-4},&x>0\end{cases}\) Determine the value of \(a\), if possible, so that the function is continuous at \(x=0\)
questions.sol: Left limit: \(\dfrac{2\sin^22x}{x^2}\to8\). Right limit: rationalising, \(\sqrt{16+\sqrt x}+4\to8\).

questions.q: A function \(f:R\to R\) satisfies the equation \(f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)\ \forall\ x,y\) in \(R\) and \(f(x)\ne0\) for any \(x\) in \(R\). Let the function be differentiable at \(x=0\) and \(f'(0)=2\). Show that \(f'(x)=2f(x)\ \forall\ x\) in \(R\). Hence determine \(f(x)\).
Find \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}\left\{\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4+x\right)\right\}^{1/x}\)
questions.sol: \(\tan\left(\frac\pi4+x\right)=\dfrac{1+\tan x}{1-\tan x}\), whose logarithm is \(\approx2\tan x\approx2x\). So the limit is \(e^2\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}(1+|\sin x|)^{a/|\sin x|},&-\dfrac\pi6<x<0\\b,&x=0\\e^{\tan2x/\tan3x},&0<x<\dfrac\pi6\end{cases}\) Determine \(a\) and \(b\) so that \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\)
questions.sol: Left limit: \((1+t)^{a/t}\to e^a\). Right limit: \(\dfrac{\tan2x}{\tan3x}\to\dfrac23\), giving \(e^{2/3}\). So \(e^a=b=e^{2/3}\).

questions.q:
Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}xe^{-\left(\frac1{|x|}+\frac1x\right)},&x\ne0\\0,&x=0\end{cases}\) Test whether
(a) \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x=0\),
(b) \(f(x)\) is differentiable \(x=0\),
questions.sol: For \(x>0\): \(f=xe^{-2/x}\); for \(x<0\): \(f=x\). Both tend to \(0\): continuous. \(\dfrac{f(h)}h\) is \(e^{-2/h}\to0\) from the right and \(1\) from the left: not differentiable.

questions.q: Let \(f\left(\dfrac{x+y}2\right)=\dfrac{f(x)+f(y)}2\) for all real \(x\) and \(y\). If \(f'(0)\) exists and \(f'(0)=-1\), \(f(0)=1\) then find \(f(2)\).
questions.sol: With \(y=0\): \(f\left(\frac x2\right)=\frac{f(x)+1}2\). Then \(f'(x)=\lim\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}h=\lim\dfrac{f(2h)-f(0)}{2h}\cdot1=f'(0)=-1\) (using \(f(x+h)=\frac{f(2x)+f(2h)}2\), \(f(x)=\frac{f(2x)+f(0)}2\)). So \(f(x)=1-x\).

questions.q: Determine the values of \(x\) for which the following function fails to be continuous or differentiable. \(f(x)=\begin{cases}1-x,&x<1\\(1-x)(2-x),&1\le x\le2\\3-x,&x>2\end{cases}\) Justify your answer.
questions.ans: Continuous and differentiable everywhere except at \(x=2\)
questions.sol: At \(1\): values \(0,0\); slopes \(-1\) and \(2x-3=-1\): differentiable. At \(2\): left value \(0\), right limit \(1\): discontinuous, hence not differentiable.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\), \(x\ge0\) be a non-negative continuous function, and let \(F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^xf(t)dt\), \(x\ge0\). If for some \(c>0\), \(f(x)\le cF(x)\) for all \(x\ge0\), then show that \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\ge0\).
questions.sol: \(F'=f\le cF\), so \(\left(e^{-cx}F(x)\right)'\le0\) and \(e^{-cx}F(x)\le F(0)=0\). But \(F\ge0\) as \(f\ge0\). So \(F\equiv0\) and \(f=F'=0\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha\in R\) prove that a function \(f:R\to R\) is differentiable at \(\alpha\) if and only if there is a function \(g:R\to R\) which is continuous at \(\alpha\) and satisfies \(f(x)-f(\alpha)=g(x)(x-\alpha)\) for all \(x\in R\).
questions.sol: If \(f\) is differentiable at \(\alpha\), define \(g(x)=\dfrac{f(x)-f(\alpha)}{x-\alpha}\) for \(x\ne\alpha\) and \(g(\alpha)=f'(\alpha)\); then \(g\) is continuous at \(\alpha\). Conversely, \(\dfrac{f(x)-f(\alpha)}{x-\alpha}=g(x)\to g(\alpha)\), so \(f'(\alpha)\) exists.

questions.q: Let \(A(t)=f_1(t)\hat i+f_2(t)\hat j\) and \(B(t)=g_1(t)\hat i+g_2(t)\hat j\), \(t\in[0,1]\) where \(f_1,f_2,g_1,g_2\) are continuous functions. If \(A(t)\) and \(B(t)\) are non-zero vectors for all \(t\) and \(A(0)=2\hat i+3\hat j\), \(A(1)=6\hat i+2\hat j\), \(B(0)=3\hat i+2\hat j\) and \(B(1)=2\hat i+6\hat j\). Then show that \(A(t)\) and \(B(t)\) are parallel for some \(t\).
questions.sol: \(h(t)=f_1g_2-f_2g_1\) is continuous with \(h(0)=4-9=-5\) and \(h(1)=36-4=32\). By the intermediate value theorem \(h(t)=0\) for some \(t\), and then the vectors are parallel.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x+a&\text{if }x<0\\|x-1|&\text{if }x\ge0\end{cases}\) and \(g(x)=\begin{cases}x+1&\text{if }x<0\\(x-1)^2+b&\text{if }x\ge0\end{cases}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are non-negative real numbers. Determine the composite function \(gof\). If \((gof)(x)\) is continuous for all real \(x\), determine the values of \(a\) and \(b\). Further, for these values of \(a\) and \(b\), is \(gof\) differentiable at \(x=0\)? Justify your answer.
questions.sol: Apply \(g\) according to the sign of \(f(x)\). Continuity at \(x=-a\): \(1=1+b\), \(b=0\). At \(x=0\): \((a-1)^2+b=b\), \(a=1\). Then \(gof=x^2\) on both sides of \(0\): differentiable there.

questions.q: If a function \(f:[-2a,2a]\to R\) is an odd function such that \(f(x)=f(2a-x)\) for \(x\in[a,2a]\) and the left hand derivative at \(x=a\) is \(0\) then find the left hand derivative at \(x=-a\).
questions.sol: LHD at \(-a\) \(=\lim\limits_{h\to0^+}\dfrac{f(-a-h)-f(-a)}{-h}=\lim\dfrac{f(a+h)-f(a)}h\) (\(f\) odd) \(=\lim\dfrac{f(a-h)-f(a)}h\) (as \(f(a+h)=f(2a-(a+h))\)) \(=-(\text{LHD at }a)=0\).

questions.q: \(P(x)\) is a polynomial function such that \(P(1)=0\), \(P'(x)>P(x)\), \(\forall\ x>1\). Prove that \(P(x)>0\), \(\forall\ x>1\)
questions.sol: \(\left(e^{-x}P(x)\right)'=e^{-x}(P'-P)>0\) for \(x>1\), so \(e^{-x}P(x)\) increases from its value \(0\) at \(x=1\).

questions.q: If \(f:[-1,1]\to R\) and \(f'(0)=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}nf\left(\dfrac1n\right)\) and \(f(0)=0\). Find the value of \(\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\dfrac2\pi(n+1)\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac1n\right)-n\). Given that \(0<\left|\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac1n\right)\right|<\dfrac\pi2\)
questions.sol: The expression is \(nf\left(\frac1n\right)\) for \(f(x)=\dfrac2\pi(1+x)\cos^{-1}x-1\), which has \(f(0)=0\). So the limit is \(f'(0)=\dfrac2\pi\left[\cos^{-1}0-1\right]=1-\dfrac2\pi\).

questions.q: \(f(x)=\begin{cases}b\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+c}2\right),&-\dfrac12\(f(x)\) is differentiable at \(x=0\) and \(|c|<1/2\), then find the value of \(a\). Also prove that \(64b^2=4-c^2\)
questions.sol: Continuity: right limit \(\frac a2=\frac12\), so \(a=1\). Right derivative: \(\lim\dfrac{\frac{e^{h/2}-1}h-\frac12}h=\dfrac18\). Left derivative: \(\dfrac b2\cdot\dfrac1{\sqrt{1-\frac{c^2}4}}=\dfrac b{\sqrt{4-c^2}}\). Equating: \(64b^2=4-c^2\).

questions.q: \(f(x)\) is a function such that \(|f(x_1)-f(x_2)|\le(x_1-x_2)^2\) and tangent at some point on \(f(x)\) passes through \((1,2)\). Find the equation of the tangent.
questions.sol: \(\left|\dfrac{f(x_1)-f(x_2)}{x_1-x_2}\right|\le|x_1-x_2|\to0\), so \(f'=0\) and \(f\) is constant. Its tangent is the horizontal line itself, and it passes through \((1,2)\).

questions.q: If two functions '\(f\)' and '\(g\)' satisfying given conditions for \(\forall\ x,y\in R\), \(f(x-y)=f(x)g(y)-f(y)\cdot g(x)\) and \(g(x-y)=g(x)\cdot g(y)+f(x)\cdot f(y)\). If right hand derivative at \(x=0\) exists for \(f(x)\) then find the derivative of \(g(x)\) at \(x=0\).
questions.sol: \(x=y\): \(f(0)=0\) and \(g(0)=g(x)^2+f(x)^2\); at \(x=0\): \(g(0)=0\) or \(1\). If \(g(0)=0\) then \(f\equiv g\equiv0\). If \(g(0)=1\): \(f(-y)=-f(y)\), so the left derivative of \(f\) at \(0\) equals the right one and \(f'(0)\) exists; differentiating \(g^2=1-f^2\) at \(0\): \(2g(0)g'(0)=-2f(0)f'(0)=0\).

questions.q: If \(\lim\limits_{x\to a}[f(x)g(x)]\) exists then both \(\lim\limits_{x\to a}f(x)\) and \(\lim\limits_{x\to a}g(x)\) exist
questions.sol: E.g. \(f(x)=x\), \(g(x)=\sin\frac1x\) at \(a=0\): the product tends to \(0\) but \(\lim g\) does not exist.

questions.q: \(\lim\limits_{x\to1}(1-x)\tan\dfrac{\pi x}2=\) ............
questions.sol: With \(h=1-x\): \(h\cot\dfrac{\pi h}2\to\dfrac2\pi\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=[x]\sin\left(\dfrac\pi{[x+1]}\right)\) where \([\cdot]\) denotes the greatest integer function. Then the domain of \(f\) is ........, points of discontinuity of \(f\) is .........
questions.ans: Domain \((-\infty,-1)\cup[0,\infty)\); discontinuous at every integer except \(0\) and \(-1\)
questions.sol: Need \([x+1]\ne0\), i.e. \(x\notin[-1,0)\). At an integer \(n\) in the domain the left and right limits are \((n-1)\sin\frac\pi n\) and \(n\sin\frac\pi{n+1}\), which differ — except at \(n=0\), where only the right side is in the domain and \(f\to0=f(0)\).

questions.q:
Let \(f_1:R\to R\), \(f_2:[0,\infty)\to R\), \(f_3:R\to R\) and \(f_4:R\to[0,\infty)\) be defined by \(f_1(x)=\begin{cases}|x|,&\text{if }x<0,\\e^x,&\text{if }x\ge0;\end{cases}\) \(f_2(x)=x^2\); \(f_3(x)=\begin{cases}\sin x,&\text{if }x<0\\x,&\text{if }x\ge0\end{cases}\) and \(f_4(x)=\begin{cases}f_2(f_1(x)),&\text{if }x<0\\f_2(f_1(x))-1,&\text{if }x\ge0\end{cases}\)
List-IList-II
P. \(f_4\) is1. onto but not one-one
Q. \(f_3\) is2. neither continuous nor one-one
R. \(f_2of_1\) is3. differentiable but not one-one
S. \(f_2\) is4. continuous and one-one
questions.sol: \(f_2of_1=x^2\) (\(x<0\)), \(e^{2x}\) (\(x\ge0\)): jumps from \(0\) to \(1\) at \(0\) and is not one-one (2). \(f_4=x^2\) (\(x<0\)), \(e^{2x}-1\) (\(x\ge0\)): range \([0,\infty)\), onto but not one-one (1). \(f_3\) has slope \(1\) on both sides of \(0\): differentiable, not one-one (3). \(f_2=x^2\) on \([0,\infty)\): continuous and one-one (4).

questions.q:
Let \(f_1:R\to R\), \(f_2:\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\to R\), \(f_3:\left(-1,e^{\frac\pi2}-2\right)\to R\), and \(f_4:R\to R\) be functions defined by
(i) \(f_1(x)=\sin\left(\sqrt{1-e^{-x^2}}\right)\),
(ii) \(f_2(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{|\sin x|}{\tan^{-1}x},&\text{if }x\ne0\\1,&\text{if }x=0\end{cases}\), where the inverse trigonometric function \(\tan^{-1}x\) assumes values in \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\),
(iii) \(f_3(x)=[\sin(\log_e(x+2))]\), where for \(t\in R\), \([t]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(t\),
(iv) \(f_4(x)=\begin{cases}x^2\sin\left(\dfrac1x\right),&\text{if }x\ne0\\0,&\text{if }x=0\end{cases}\).
List-IList-II
P. The function \(f_1\) is1. NOT continuous at \(x=0\)
Q. The function \(f_2\) is2. continuous at \(x=0\) and NOT differentiable at \(x=0\)
R. The function \(f_3\) is3. differentiable at \(x=0\) and its derivative is NOT continuous at \(x=0\)
S. The function \(f_4\) is4. differentiable at \(x=0\) and its derivative is continuous at \(x=0\)
The correct option is:
questions.sol: \(f_1\approx\sqrt{1-e^{-x^2}}\approx|x|\) near \(0\): continuous, not differentiable (2). \(f_2\to\pm1\) from the two sides: not continuous (1). On its domain \(\log_e(x+2)\in\left(0,\frac\pi2\right)\), so \(f_3\equiv0\) (4). \(f_4'(0)=0\) but \(f_4'(x)=2x\sin\frac1x-\cos\frac1x\) has no limit (3).

questions.q:
Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be functions defined by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x|x|\sin\left(\dfrac1x\right),&x\ne0,\\0,&x=0,\end{cases}\) and \(g(x)=\begin{cases}1-2x,&0\le x\le\dfrac12,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\)
Let \(a,b,c,d\in\mathbb R\). Define the function \(h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) by \(h(x)=af(x)+b\left(g(x)+g\left(\dfrac12-x\right)\right)+c(x-g(x))+dg(x)\), \(x\in\mathbb R\)
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) If \(a=0\), \(b=1\), \(c=0\), and \(d=0\), then(1) \(h\) is one-one
(Q) If \(a=1\), \(b=0\), \(c=0\), and \(d=0\), then(2) \(h\) is onto.
(R) If \(a=0\), \(b=0\), \(c=1\), and \(d=0\), then(3) \(h\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb R\)
(S) If \(a=0\), \(b=0\), \(c=0\), and \(d=1\), then(4) the range of \(h\) is \([0,1]\).
(5) the range of \(h\) is \(\{0,1\}\).
The correct option is:
questions.sol: (P) \(g(x)+g\left(\frac12-x\right)=(1-2x)+2x=1\) on \(\left[0,\frac12\right]\) and \(0\) elsewhere: range \(\{0,1\}\). (Q) \(h=f\): \(\dfrac{f(x)}x=|x|\sin\frac1x\to0\), differentiable on \(\mathbb R\). (R) \(h=x-g(x)\) is \(x\) outside \(\left[0,\frac12\right]\) and \(3x-1\) inside: it covers all of \(\mathbb R\) (onto) but is not one-one. (S) \(h=g\) has range \([0,1]\).

Let \(f\) and \(g\) be real valued functions defined on interval \((-1,1)\) such that \(g''(x)\) is continuous, \(g(0)\ne0\), \(g'(0)=0\), \(g''(0)\ne0\) and \(f(x)=g(x)\sin x\).
Statement - 1 : \(\lim\limits_{x\to0}[g(x)\cot x-g(0)\text{cosec}\,x]=f''(0)\).
Statement - 2 : \(f'(0)=g(0)\).
opts: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is a correct explanation of Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is False
Statement-1 is False, Statement-2 is True.
questions.sol: \(f'=g'\sin x+g\cos x\), so \(f'(0)=g(0)\). \(f''=g''\sin x+2g'\cos x-g\sin x\), so \(f''(0)=2g'(0)=0\). The limit is \(\lim\dfrac{g(x)\cos x-g(0)}{\sin x}=\lim\dfrac{g'\cos x-g\sin x}{\cos x}=g'(0)=0\). Both are true, but Statement-2 does not explain Statement-1. (The book prints the limit as \(x\to\infty\).)

questions.q: Let the functions \(f:(-1,1)\to R\) and \(g:(-1,1)\to(-1,1)\) be defined by \(f(x)=|2x-1|+|2x+1|\) and \(g(x)=x-[x]\), where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\). Let \(fog:(-1,1)\to R\) be the composite function defined by \((fog)(x)=f(g(x))\). Suppose \(c\) is the number of points in the interval \((-1,1)\) at which \(fog\) is NOT continuous, and suppose \(d\) is the number of points in the interval \((-1,1)\) at which \(fog\) is NOT differentiable. Then the value of \(c+d\) is _____
questions.sol: For \(t=g(x)\in[0,1)\): \(f(t)=2\) if \(t<\frac12\), \(4t\) if \(t\ge\frac12\). So \(fog=2\) on \(\left(-1,-\frac12\right)\), \(4(x+1)\) on \(\left[-\frac12,0\right)\), \(2\) on \(\left[0,\frac12\right)\), \(4x\) on \(\left[\frac12,1\right)\). Discontinuous only at \(0\) (\(c=1\)); not differentiable at \(-\frac12,0,\frac12\) (\(d=3\)).

questions.q: The value of the limit \(\lim\limits_{x\to\frac\pi2}\dfrac{4\sqrt2(\sin3x+\sin x)}{\left(2\sin2x\sin\dfrac{3x}2+\cos\dfrac{5x}2\right)-\left(\sqrt2+\sqrt2\cos2x+\cos\dfrac{3x}2\right)}\) is _____
questions.sol: Put \(x=\frac\pi2-h\) and expand to order \(h^2\). Numerator: \(4\sqrt2\cdot2\sin2x\cos x=16\sqrt2\sin x\cos^2x\approx16\sqrt2h^2\). Denominator: the constant and first-order terms cancel and it is \(\approx2\sqrt2h^2\). Limit \(\dfrac{16\sqrt2}{2\sqrt2}=8\).

questions.q: Let \(e\) denote the base of the natural logarithm. The value of the real number \(a\) for which the right hand limit \(\lim\limits_{x\to0^+}\dfrac{(1-x)^{1/x}-e^{-1}}{x^a}\) is equal to a non-zero real, is _____.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1x\ln(1-x)=-1-\dfrac x2-\ldots\), so \((1-x)^{1/x}=e^{-1}\left(1-\dfrac x2+\ldots\right)\). The numerator is \(\approx-\dfrac x{2e}\): \(a=1\).

questions.q: If \(\beta=\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{e^{x^3}-(1-x^3)^{1/3}+\left((1-x^2)^{1/2}-1\right)\sin x}{x\sin^2x}\) then the value of \(6\beta\) is _____.
questions.sol: To order \(x^3\): \(e^{x^3}-(1-x^3)^{1/3}\approx x^3+\dfrac{x^3}3\) and \(\left(\sqrt{1-x^2}-1\right)\sin x\approx-\dfrac{x^3}2\). \(\beta=\dfrac43-\dfrac12=\dfrac56\).
